PTE vs IELTS for Australia PR

Choosing between PTE and IELTS is one of the most important decisions for your Australia PR application. The right test can make the difference between 10 points and 20 points for English.

Which Should You Choose?

Choose PTE If:

  • You struggle with IELTS writing but type well
  • You feel nervous speaking to an examiner
  • You need fast results
  • You are comfortable with computers

Choose IELTS If:

  • You prefer face-to-face speaking tests
  • You write better by hand
  • Your preparation has focused on IELTS format
  • You prefer a well-known, established test

Pro Tips

  • Try both practice tests before committing to one
  • Focus on your weakest section — your overall level is limited by it
  • Retake if close — even one section at the next level adds 10 points
  • Time your test carefully — results must be valid when invited

Frequently Asked Questions

Is PTE easier than IELTS for Australia PR?
Many applicants find PTE easier, especially for writing and speaking. PTE uses automated scoring and computer-based delivery, which some prefer. However, individual results vary — take practice tests for both before deciding.
What PTE score equals IELTS 8.0 for Superior English?
PTE 79 in each section equals IELTS 8.0 in each band for Superior English (20 points). PTE 65 equals IELTS 7.0 for Proficient English (10 points). PTE 50 equals IELTS 6.0 for Competent English (0 points).
Can I take both PTE and IELTS?
Yes. Both are accepted for skilled migration. You can take whichever gives you a better result and use it for your application. Some applicants take both tests and submit the better score.
How long does it take to get PTE results vs IELTS?
PTE results are typically available within 2-5 business days. IELTS paper-based takes 13 days, while IELTS computer-delivered takes 3-5 days. This faster turnaround makes PTE attractive for time-sensitive applications.
Does Australia immigration accept TOEFL for PR?
As of 2026, IELTS, PTE Academic, TOEFL iBT, and Cambridge English are accepted. However, always verify current acceptance on the Department of Home Affairs website before booking a test, as policies can change.
